 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What are the two main minerals that make water hard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium and Calcium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hard water is primarily caused by the presence of **magnesium (Mg²⁺) and calcium (Ca²⁺) ions** dissolved in water.
 
• These minerals originate from deposits of **limestone, chalk, and dolomite**, which are rich in calcium carbonate and magnesium carbonate.
 
• The concentration of these ions is measured in terms of water hardness, typically expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L) or parts per million (ppm).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron and sulfur**

 
 
• Presence of iron can cause reddish stains, and sulfur causes rotten egg smell in water.
 
• Common in groundwater with high mineral content.
 
 
 
• **Gypsum and Manganese**
 
 
• Gypsum (CaSO₄) contributes to permanent hardness, but manganese mainly affects taste and staining.
 
• Manganese-rich water often looks brown or black.
 
 
 
• **Sodium and Potassium**
 
 
• These do not cause hardness; they are soft minerals.
 
• Softening processes often replace Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ with Na⁺ ions.

questions.question: In March 2020, the Government of India increased the MSP for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops by _______ return to the weighted average cost of production for India's agricultural years 2018-19 and 2019-20.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India, in March 2020, increased the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all mandated Kharif, Rabi, and other commercial crops to ensure a **minimum 50% return (1.5 times)** over the weighted average cost of production.
 
• This initiative aligns with the recommendations of the **Swaminathan Commission, **which suggested fixing MSP at least 1.5 times the cost of production for better profitability for farmers.
 
• The increased MSP covers a wide range of crops, including **cereals, pulses, oilseeds, and commercial crops like cotton and sugarcane**, ensuring equitable benefits across agricultural sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minimum Support Price (MSP):**

 
 
• MSP is a form of market intervention by the Government of India to safeguard farmers from sharp price fluctuations in agricultural commodities.
 
• It is announced by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs **based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
 
 
 
• **Swaminathan Commission:**
 
 
• The National Commission on Farmers (**NCF**), chaired by M.S. Swaminathan, suggested measures to improve farm profitability and sustainability.
 
• One of its key recommendations was fixing MSP at **1.5 times** the cost of production to ensure fair returns to farmers.

questions.question: According to Budget 2020, all income below Rs. _____ per year will be tax-free.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹5 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Union Budget 2020, the government announced that individuals earning an annual income of up to ₹5 lakh would not be required to pay income tax.
 
• This relief was provided under** Section 87A** of the Income Tax Act, which allows a rebate for individuals with income below the specified threshold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budget:**

 
 
• Annual financial statement of the Government of India presenting estimated receipts and expenditures for the next financial year (April–March).
 
• **Article 112 **of the Indian Constitution mandates the President to lay before Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures.
 
 
 
• **Components**:
 
 
• Revenue Budget: Includes revenue receipts (tax & non-tax) and revenue expenditure.
 
• Capital Budget: Includes capital receipts (borrowings, loans) and capital expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Types of Budgets:**
 
 
• Union Budget – Prepared by the Central Government.
 
• State Budget – Prepared by respective State Governments.
 
• Supplementary/Extraordinary Budget – Introduced if extra funds are needed mid-year.
 
 
 
• **Preparation and Presentation:**
 
 
• Prepared by the Finance Ministry, headed by the Finance Minister.
 
• Typically presented on **1st February** (since 2017; earlier 28th February) in Parliament.

questions.question: The first co-operative society in India was formed in ______ state.

• This society was set up under the provisions of the **Cooperative Societies Act of 1904**, which was introduced to promote cooperative principles and self-help among rural communities.
 
• The society was primarily aimed at providing **credit facilities to farmers** and protecting them from exploitation by moneylenders.
 
• Karnataka, particularly the districts of Dharwad and Gadag, played a pioneering role in the **cooperative movement in India**.

questions.question:
Which article of the Constitution of India states the following?

"An amendment of this Constitution may be brought into force only by the introduction of a bill in either House of Parliament."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution provides the procedure for the amendment of the Constitution.
 
• It states that an amendment to the Constitution can be initiated only by introducing a Bill in either House of Parliament** (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha).**
 
• The amendment Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Amendments in the Constitution:**

 
 
• **Simple Majority Amendments:** These amendments can be passed by a simple majority of the members present and voting in the Parliament, e.g., changes to the 7th Schedule or the creation of new states.
 
• **Special Majority Amendments:** These require a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in addition to the majority of the total membership of each House.
 
• **Special Majority with State Ratification:** Certain amendments require ratification by at least half of the state legislatures, e.g., changes to federal provisions.
 
 
 
• **Key Examples of Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, is known as the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the extensive changes it brought to the Constitution.
 
• The** 73rd and 74th** Amendment Acts introduced Panchayati Raj and Urban Local Bodies to strengthen decentralized governance.

questions.question: Which rule of 'Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha' explains the dilatory motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rule 230**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rule 230** of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Rajya Sabha deals specifically with dilatory motions.
 
• A **dilatory motion** is used to **postpone or delay** the discussion or decision on a particular matter under consideration.
 
• The rule allows members to move such motions, but the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has the authority to either accept or reject them based on relevance and necessity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule 230**

 
 
• Deals with closure of debate (similar to “guillotine”) to ensure timely disposal of business.
 
• Enables the House to vote on a question without further discussion.
 
 
 
• **Rule 231**
 
 
• Provides procedure for moving an amendment to a bill or motion.
 
• Ensures that amendments are relevant and within scope of the original motion.
 
 
 
• **Rule 243**
 
 
• Relates to suspension or adjournment of business for certain administrative reasons.
 
• Gives Chairman authority to maintain order and schedule of proceedings.

questions.question: What is the fiscal deficit target of India for 2019-20?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.0459**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The fiscal deficit target for India in the financial year 2019-20 was **3.3% of the GDP**, which translates to approximately **0.0459**.
 
• The fiscal deficit represents the difference between the government’s total expenditure and revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• It indicates the amount by which the government needs to borrow to meet its expenditure requirements.
 
• For 2019-20, the fiscal deficit target was reduced from the previous year's target of 3.4% to **3.3% of GDP**, showcasing the government's intention to ensure fiscal prudence.
 
• This target was announced during the Union Budget 2019-20, presented by the then Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**

 
 
• Fiscal deficit is calculated as the difference between total expenditure and total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• It is a key indicator of the financial health of the government and shows its reliance on borrowing to meet expenses.
 
• The government aims to gradually reduce the fiscal deficit to achieve sustainable economic growth.
 
 
 
• **GDP:**
 
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
 
• Fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP helps to compare the borrowing needs with the size of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget:**
 
 
• The Union Budget is the annual financial statement presented by the Government of India, detailing revenue and expenditure for the upcoming fiscal year.
 
• It includes fiscal targets such as fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and primary deficit.
 
 
 
• **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy:**
 
 
• India follows a medium-term fiscal policy to gradually reduce fiscal deficit targets as part of its long-term economic strategy.
 
• The goal is to maintain fiscal discipline while ensuring sufficient allocation for growth and development.

questions.question: Which of the following agencies announced the SunRISE mission in 2020 to explore the point where massive particles are generated on the Sun and evolve as they expand into space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NASA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NASA announced the SunRISE mission in March 2020**, aimed at studying solar particle generation and their evolution as they expand into space.
 
• The SunRISE mission stands for **Sun Radio Interferometer Space Experiment**, which will use six CubeSats to create a 3D map of solar radio emissions.
 
• The mission's primary goal is to understand how solar storms occur and potentially improve warnings about space weather hazards.
 
• The six CubeSats will work together as a large radio telescope to detect and analyze low-frequency radio waves emitted by the Sun.
 
• The information gathered will help scientists better understand how solar particle storms impact the Earth and spacecraft operating in space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CubeSats:**

 
 
• CubeSats are miniature satellites used for space research and exploration.
 
• The SunRISE mission uses six CubeSats to operate collaboratively as an array for radio frequency detection.
 
• These satellites are cost-effective and often used for specific scientific experiments.
 
 
 
• **Space Weather:**
 
 
• Space weather refers to conditions caused by solar activity, such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections.
 
• These phenomena can disrupt satellites, communication systems, and power grids on Earth.
 
• The SunRISE mission aims to predict such events more accurately to mitigate risks.
 
 
 
• **Solar Particle Storms:**
 
 
• Solar particle storms are high-energy particles released during solar explosions.
 
• They pose a threat to astronauts, spacecraft, and Earth's technological systems.
 
• The SunRISE mission seeks to map the origin and behavior of these storms.
 
 
 
• **Radio Emissions:**
 
 
• Radio waves emitted by the Sun provide important clues about solar activity.
 
• The SunRISE mission's 3D mapping of radio emissions will help identify where solar storms start.

questions.question: How many drops of OPV vaccine per dose does the World Health Organization (WHO) recommend?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends **two drops** of the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) per dose.
 
• OPV is a live attenuated (weakened) vaccine administered orally to protect against poliomyelitis (polio).
 
• The two-drop dose is designed to provide sufficient antigen exposure to stimulate the immune system effectively in children.
 
• OPV is administered several times as part of routine immunization schedules and polio eradication campaigns to ensure sustained immunity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV):**

 
 
• OPV contains live attenuated poliovirus strains of all three serotypes (type 1, type 2, and type 3).
 
• It is administered orally, making it easy to use during mass immunization campaigns.
 
• OPV provides both systemic and intestinal immunity, which is crucial in halting virus transmission.
 
 
 
• **Poliomyelitis (Polio):**
 
 
• Polio is a highly infectious viral disease that primarily affects young children.
 
• The virus is transmitted through contaminated water or food and multiplies in the intestine, potentially causing paralysis.
 
• Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent polio.
 
 
 
• **Polio Eradication Efforts:**
 
 
• The Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) was launched in 1988 to eliminate polio worldwide.
 
• Mass immunization campaigns using OPV have significantly reduced polio cases globally.
 
• Countries like India were declared polio-free due to sustained vaccination efforts.
 
 
 
• **Other Vaccines for Polio:**
 
 
• In addition to OPV, the Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) is also used, which contains inactivated (killed) poliovirus.
 
• IPV is administered via injection and provides systemic immunity but not intestinal immunity.
 
• Many countries use a combination of OPV and IPV for comprehensive polio protection.

questions.question: What will be the effect on the boiling point of water when salt is added to it?

options.text: It will first increase and then decrease

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It will increase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Adding salt to water increases its boiling point due to a phenomenon called **boiling point elevation**.
 
• When salt dissolves in water, it separates into ions, which disrupt the formation of vapor, requiring a higher temperature to boil.
 
• This is a colligative property, which depends on the number of solute particles in the solution rather than their identity.
 
• Boiling point elevation occurs because the salt ions lower the water's vapor pressure, making it harder for water molecules to escape into the gas phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colligative Properties:**

 
 
• These are properties of solutions that depend on the concentration of solute particles, not their identity.
 
• Examples include boiling point elevation, freezing point depression, vapor pressure lowering, and osmotic pressure.
 
 
 
• **Boiling Point Elevation Formula:**
 
 
• The increase in boiling point can be calculated using the formula:** ΔTb = i × Kb × m.**
 
• Here, ΔTb is the boiling point elevation, i is the van't Hoff factor (number of ions formed by dissociation), Kb is the boiling point elevation constant, and m is the molality of the solution.
 
 
 
• **Salt Dissociation:**
 
 
• When salt **(NaCl)** dissolves in water, it dissociates into sodium (Na⁺) and chloride (Cl−) ions.
 
• These ions disrupt the intermolecular forces between water molecules, altering its physical properties.
 
 
 
• **Vapor Pressure and Boiling Point:**
 
 
• Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the external atmospheric pressure.
 
• Adding salt lowers the vapor pressure, requiring a higher temperature to reach boiling point.
